# "Holding simultaneous elections would be convenient for EC and nation": JPC Chief PP Chaudhary reiterates support for ONOE

## Chairman of the Joint Parliamentary Committee (JPC) on 'One Nation, One Election' and BJP MP PP Chaudhary highlighted a series of reports and recommendations supporting simultaneous elections, saying the idea has been discussed for decades and is in the national interest.

[ANI](/ani-stories)
| India

Image Credit: ANI

Chairman of the Joint Parliamentary Committee (JPC) on 'One Nation, One Election' and BJP MP PP Chaudhary reiterated that the idea of having simultaneous elections is in the national interest while highlighting that the idea has been discussed for decades, pointing to a series of reports and recommendations supporting simultaneous elections. Speaking to ANI, Chaudhary said on Sunday that the Election Commission of India (ECI) in 1983 and a former Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee committee in 2002 backed simultaneous elections to ease the electoral burden.

"As early as 1983, the Election Commission of India acknowledged the burden of constant engagement in the electoral process and noted that holding simultaneous elections would be convenient for both the Commission and the nation. Subsequently, a committee on the 'Working of the Constitution,' established by Atal Bihari Vajpayee, recommended in its 2002 report that simultaneous elections should be held nationwide," Chaudhary told ANI. Chaudhary added, "This was followed by report

# Putin Threatens Retaliation After Ukrainian Drone Strikes

Russia and Ukraine escalate attacks on each other's critical economic infrastructure, raising global concerns over food and energy supply chains.

## Key Points

Russian President Vladimir Putin has sharply escalated rhetoric and threatened retaliation after a wave of Ukrainian drone strikes targeted Russia’s economic infrastructure, signaling a dangerous new phase in the ongoing conflict. In a state television interview aired on August 22, 2026, and widely reported by outlets such as Reuters and Russia’s own Vesti, Putin accused Ukraine of having “opened Pandora’s box” by striking at Russia’s vital economic assets with unmanned aerial vehicles.

Putin’s comments came in the wake of a summer marked by intensified Ukrainian drone attacks on Russian soil, with particular focus on oil refining facilities and the logistics warehouses of major online retailers. The most notable incident occurred on August 16, when a Ukrainian drone strike damaged a logistics warehouse belonging to Wildberries, Russia’s largest e-commerce company, in Koledino, Moscow region. According to Russian authorities, this was just one of several attacks on Wildberries’ logistics infrastructure in recent weeks.

“Ukraine has opened Pandora’s box by targeting Russian civilian companies and attempting to destroy the Russian economy,” Putin declared in the televised interview, as reported by Vesti and Reuters.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said Russia was "not ready" ​for a ceasefire on attacks on ships in ​the Black Sea carrying agricultural ‌produce, ​as Moscow wants to extend any deal to cover attacks on Russian refineries and pipelines. Russia dismissed the idea, saying it saw no grounds for "half-measures" that would ‌offer a respite to the other side. "I spoke with certain leaders. # Yemen's government-aligned forces say they repelled Houthi drones west of Aden

Drones intercepted before reaching their targets, Southern Armed Forces say

Mohammed Sameai and Serdar Dincel

24 August 2026•Update: 24 August 2026

![Content media](https://web-cdnprod.aa.com.tr/uploads/Contents/2026/08/24/thumbs_b_c_48f2a7c8dd1c1376cee8327f560c4926.jpg)

YEMEN/ISTANBUL

Yemen's internationally recognized government-aligned forces said early Monday that they intercepted “hostile Houthi drones” west of the southern city of Aden, the country’s interim capital.

The Southern Armed Forces, led by Presidential Leadership Council member Abdul Rahman al-Muharrami, said on the US social media company X that the drones were intercepted before reaching their targets, without providing further details.

The forces did not specify the source of the drones or the outcome of the interception operation.

The Houthis did not immediately comment on the statement.

Yemen had been under a relative lull since April 2022 after nearly 12 years of war between government forces, backed by a Saudi-led coalition, and the Iran-backed Houthis, who seized control of the capital Sanaa, and large parts of the country in 2014.
